news.title: Intel gets waiver after worries fuzzy US ban on foreign-made robots may hit fabs
paras: Intel, a big chip maker, needed a waiver so it could keep using foreign robots. The U.S. government almost banned all robots made overseas, but Intel asked for an exception. The Federal Communications Commission gave Intel permission for one year.

These robots help move parts in chip factories. Without them, building chips would be slower and more expensive. Because Intel wanted to stay safe from new rules, it gets the waiver. Now it can keep robots moving parts through its factories and keep technology ready.

news.title: Atlas Robot’s New Hand May Outperform Humanlike Designs
paras: Robots need a hand that can pick, move, and grip objects easily to help them work in real life. Building such a hand is very hard because it must be strong, flexible, and simple to make. Boston Dynamics says their new robot hand should have three fingers and one thumb.

The hand needs 13 degrees of freedom, meaning 13 movable joints. These joints let the robot grasp objects in many ways, just like a human hand. Because of this design, the robot can pick delicate items without crushing them, making it safer for people.

news.title: SpaceX launches Starlink satellites from California as Falcon 9 cadence slows (photos)
paras: The spacecraft, Starlink Group 15-15, were stacked 27 high inside the payload fairing of a SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket , which lifted off from Pad 4E at Vandenberg Space Force Base at 6:48 p.m. The rocket's first stage booster, designated B1063, executed its main engine cutoff and stage separation about 2.5 minutes into flight, sending the second stage to continue onward to low Earth orbit (LEO).

The vehicle's two-piece protective payload fairing was jettisoned just before T+3 minutes. The booster, meanwhile, reoriented for its descent back to Earth. The Falcon 9's upper stage completed its first engine burn shortly after B1063 landed and will coast for about 45 minutes before initiating a second and final orbital insertion burn.

news.title: Is Taekwondo an art or A Sport?
paras: And then… silence, and then someone from the crowd shouted… “Is Taekwondo a sport or is it a performing arts?” Well we are here to answer that question! Did you know that Taekwondo is Korean? In Korean, chung and hung mean blue and red.

They use these colours to represent a competitor at a competition. You wear protective gear in that colour on your stomach. Otherwise, you wear your own white gear. According to sources such as The Korea Herald and Kiddle, Taekwondo is a form of performing art, because you don’t just fight, you learn a pattern.

news.title: Zoo animals enjoy spooktacular Halloween treats
paras: Animals at Whipsnade Zoo are enjoying an early taste of Halloween with some special treats. The lemurs and macaques tucked into carved pumpkins to find sweetcorn and peppers, whilst rhino Hugo enjoyed his usual breakfast of hay and cabbage.

The zoo's keepers been trying to find creative ways to encourage the animals' natural instincts to hunt and explore. Matthew Webb, Head of Zoological Operations at Whipsnade Zoo, said: "As everyone counts down to Halloween, our zookeepers used seasonal squashes to make sure the animals don't miss out on any of the fun"

sport.title: ‘Staying healthy is a real skill’: Mouratoglou explains why Zverev deserves to be No. 1
paras: Patrick Mouratoglou believes Alexander Zverev fully deserves his No. 1 ranking, even if Jannik Sinner and Carlos Alcaraz are better players.

Staying healthy, he argues, is “a real skill” that demands sacrifice, and Zverev’s two Grand Slam titles in 2026 marked a mental breakthrough. Alexander Zverev may not be the best player in the world, but his ranking is fully deserved. That is Patrick Mouratoglou’s view, set out in a video on his social media channels in which he argued that staying healthy is a skill in itself, and part of a player’s value.

sport.title: October 24, 1999: The day Amelie Mauresmo claimed her first WTA singles title
paras: On this day in tennis history, two young budding superstars faced off and it was Mauresmo who won her maiden crown On this day, October 24, 1999, a 20-year-old Amelie Mauresmo claimed her maiden title in Bratislava, defeating another rising star in 16-year-old Kim Clijsters (6-3, 6-3).

It was the first of 15 clashes between two future world No 1s, and, for the French player, the first of the 25 singles titles that she would win throughout her career. She was successful at a young age, winning in the juniors rank at both Roland-Garros and Wimbledon in 1996.

sport.title: Venus Williams confirmed to play opponent 28 years younger than her in first match since the US Open
paras: Venus Williams will make her return to competition at the Guangzhou Open. Williams last competed at the US Open , where she lost her 15th consecutive singles match after losing to Sofia Kenin in the first round.

Venus also lost her only doubles match at the US Open alongside her younger sister Serena , with many assuming that this would be the end of the season for the 46-year-old. It then came as a surprise when it was announced that Venus Williams would be competing at the WTA 250 tournament in Guangzhou, where her singles draw has now been confirmed.

sport.title: Carlos Alcaraz’s plan ahead of the Vienna Open has now been revealed including his two practice partners
paras: It feels like some time since we last saw Carlos Alcaraz on court, following his surprise early dismissal from the Shanghai Masters. His loss at the hands of Zizou Bergs came as a great shock to the tennis world, as his struggles around this period of the season threatened to emerge once again.

Clearly keen to ensure that he does not fall victim to a similar issue at the Paris Masters, Alcaraz has since taken a wildcard at the Vienna Open , where he will play next week. With that in mind, his plan in the lead-up to this ATP 500 event has been revealed, including two rather star-studded practice partners.

sport.title: Alex Eala confirmed to play British player in the first round of the Tokyo Open as her draw is revealed
paras: Alex Eala will play the penultimate tournament of her 2026 season by making her debut at the Tokyo Open. Eala has enjoyed the best season of her career so far this year, having won her first WTA title at the Washington Open , reached the fourth round of Wimbledon and broken into the top 20.

Despite all of her success, Eala will not be a part of the WTA Finals this year and therefore only has two tournaments left to play in Tokyo and Hong Kong. Eala was beaten by Diana Shnaider in Ningbo , and she could face the Russian once again after the Tokyo Open draw was announced.

sport.title: ATP Lyon Best Bets Including Tommy Paul Vs Taylor Fritz
paras: This is a 250-point tournament, so this is not a centerpiece portion of the run-up to the ATP Finals in Turin, Italy. ATP Lyon is an event suited for European players who didn’t do much in the fall Asian swing and who want to regroup closer to home.

There are bigger European tournaments coming up in the next few weeks, so Lyon is a tune-up event for those larger touranments. European pros want to get some rhythm so that they can build up form going into the next few weeks of the season, which represent the last few weeks of the ATP Tour season.
